criterionFindings.criterion: Captured bytes are hash-verified and never executed; captured text is not emitted
criterionFindings.basis: Source: buildBoundarySurface reads each manifest file, recomputes SHA-256 and refuses with private_analysis_evidence_drift on any mismatch (boundary-surface.ts:544-549); the module contains no execution machinery (no vm/eval/child_process; the only eval/Function/worker references are detection patterns). Stored projections contain only paths, resolved paths, specifier texts, syntactic kinds, short identifier chains and positions; statement bodies, string payload values and file bytes are never emitted. Re-run observed: journey and hostile-input tests assert the canary string, JSON secret values, host temp paths and drift text never appear in the serialized surface.

criterionFindings.criterion: Revision integrity: the review binds the exact declared revision digest
criterionFindings.basis: I recomputed the M3.1 revision manifest per scripts/execution.mjs (write paths + shared paths + integration paths, per-file SHA-256, localeCompare en, compact canonical JSON) and reproduced digest 7fe68431dfd8815027e8accdd951b7b76e813cbb1cf98c66e73ae1ce56435824 with 0 missing / 0 added / 0 changed files against the stored manifest; taskDefinitionSha256 matches tasks/task-graph.json.

limitations: Static-analysis limits disclosed in ANALYSIS_LIMITS are inherent: aliases, decorators, generics, conditional runtime paths and variable-mediated dataflow are not interpreted, so a missed dynamic site would be undetected rather than misclassified; detection is conservative in the safe direction (unknown/computed) but not exhaustive.

Import classifications include a literal 'safe' label for statically resolved in-manifest, non-private runtime imports, and private-to-private internal imports are structurally 'safe'; privacy enforcement between processes is a runtime ACL concern, not an AST one. The 'private' marker is a path-segment heuristic ('private' segment), disclosed in the draft.

boundary.nestedWorker stores the worker script argument text (a specifier-class value, e.g. a synthetic worker file name) consistent with the disclosed specifier-text projection surface; it is the one captured string literal family emitted into the report.
Omitted-state detection walks only top-level exported function declarations and exported arrow bindings; class members and nested closures are not walked (disclosed in ANALYSIS_LIMITS and the draft).
